findings.text: Journal state keeps a fixed size checkpoint batch array that was moved out of the checkpoint path to save stack, together with a shrinker handle and a per CPU tally of checkpoint queued buffers plus a pointer to the next transaction the shrinker will visit.

Log position uses a head marking the earliest free slot and a tail marking the earliest live slot with a free count and usable interval bounds, alongside a separate fast commit interval with its own start and end plus a currently allocated length that is only touched by the lone fast commit actor.

Storage binding records the journal device with block size and start offset and printable name, plus the client filesystem device with sampled write error sequence and total region capacity and atomic reserved credit count and optional inode for block mapping and filesystem private pointer and object identifier bytes with derived checksum seed, where internal journals alias both devices.

Progress uses four transaction numbers for oldest live and next to grant and most recently completed and most recently requested, with a dedicated commit thread and timer and interval and per transaction buffer ceiling and revocation density and bookkeeping overhead and batch delay window and average commit duration and last synchronous writer identity and failed commit marker plus aggregate statistics.

Checkpoint batch access serialises on j_checkpoint_mutex and buffer lists with checkpoint counts and shrink target on j_list_lock and head tail free counts with geometry and sequence numbers and average duration on j_state_lock and history on j_history_lock with revocation structures on j_revoke_lock, while fast commit allocation offset and fast commit batch storage assume a lone committer and need no lock and two sequence values permit lock free racy peeks.

Trigger descriptor carries two callbacks, one run when data destined for the log becomes stable with a mapped frozen image and length, and the other run if abort discards dirty content that will miss commit.

Per buffer wrapper links back to its buffer and counts references and selects a journaling queue and records whether the running transaction dirtied it, and it keeps a frozen image for logging with a clean image lacking uncommitted removals and tracks owning and successor transactions and chains buffers on transaction queues and on checkpoint queues with a checkpoint owner plus live and frozen trigger associations.

Back pointer and reference tally sit under the journal head lock and queue selector with dirty marker and frozen and clean images sit under b_state_lock, while owner is readable under either j_list_lock or b_state_lock but writable under both and successor with transaction chaining needs t_list_lock plus b_state_lock and checkpoint owner with checkpoint chaining needs j_list_lock.
Transaction identity is a wide unsigned value with wraparound ordering, and the compound transaction name aliases an incomplete record type defined elsewhere.
Both examined headers employ a single inclusion guard that expands empty to ensure one time processing.

Control flags use distinct powers of two with JBD2_UNMOUNT as one for thread teardown and JBD2_ABORT as two for error shutdown and JBD2_ACK_ERR as four for error acknowledgement and JBD2_FLUSHED as eight for superblock flush and JBD2_LOADED as sixteen for superblock load and JBD2_BARRIER as thirty two for barrier use and JBD2_CYCLE_RECORD as one hundred twenty eight for empty log cycling and JBD2_FAST_COMMIT_ONGOING as two hundred fifty six while fast commit runs and JBD2_FULL_COMMIT_ONGOING as five hundred twelve while full commit runs.
Flush mode uses JBD2_JOURNAL_FLUSH_DISCARD as one for discard and JBD2_JOURNAL_FLUSH_ZEROOUT as two for zeroing, with JBD2_JOURNAL_FLUSH_VALID as their union marking allowed modes.
Journal input output requests combine REQ_META with REQ_SYNC and REQ_IDLE to request metadata handling with synchronous idle priority.

Buffer queue selector uses BJ_None as zero for unjournaled and BJ_Metadata as one for regular metadata and BJ_Forget as two for superseded forget and BJ_Shadow as three for shadowed log copy and BJ_Reserved as four for reserved access, with BJ_Types as five counting the kinds.

Default revocation hash size named JOURNAL_REVOKE_DEFAULT_HASH is two hundred fifty six buckets, and shrinker outcome enumerates JBD2_SHRINK_DESTROY first then JBD2_SHRINK_BUSY_STOP then JBD2_SHRINK_BUSY_SKIP.

Superblock version test treats first generation layout as lacking extended features, while three factories each emit per feature presence test plus enable and disable helpers operating on compat and read only compat and incompat words with endian translation and version gating.
Commit wait annotation briefly takes then drops the transaction commit dependency tracker to inform lock validation without sleeping.
Logging attaches a buffer association link at the tail of a chosen list, and detaching removes that link while resetting it for reuse.

Current transaction handle is obtained from the running task control record, journal failure is detected from its control word abort bit, handle failure adds handle marked state or missing transaction, and a setter marks a handle failed.
Initialisation samples the client device address space write error cursor into journal memory, and checking compares live cursor against the sampled value using a single volatile read.
Identifier ordering subtracts then tests sign, yielding greater and greater or equal that remain correct across wrap.
Checksum support is true when either second or third generation capability is present, and fast commit capacity reads an on disk count falling back to a built in default when zero.

Usable log estimate starts from free count minus a thirty two block rounding reserve and subtracts outstanding credits of any committing transaction and floors at zero, latest identifier is read under shared state protection preferring the running transaction else the last request, and handle allowance deducts rounded up revocation demand using per block density with journal chosen by reservation state.
Handle objects are taken zeroed and inode wrappers untracked from dedicated caches with matching releases, and running checksum folds arbitrary bytes via a cyclic code.
All buffer and journal diagnostic macros accept their usual arguments but expand to empty statements, so tracing calls have no runtime effect in this build.

Replay proceeds block by block with callee votes to continue and halt at end or fail with negative status, while each buffer occupies one journaling queue among unjournaled and metadata and forget and shadow and reserved.

Transaction numbers advance monotonically with wrap comparison, from oldest retained through requested and running toward next grant, while completed marker trails and latest query resolves to running when present.
Lock free peeks at commit progress can observe stale values, and fast commit allocation offset plus batch arrays assume a lone actor so concurrent use would corrupt accounting.

Merging queue selector with dirty marker into one bitfield is forbidden because wide accesses could clobber the adjacent reference tally under concurrent modification, and frozen versus live trigger pointers must not be interchanged.
